title: ALMA FACTS. II. Large Scale Variations in the <SUP>12</SUP>CO(J = 2 ─ 1) to <SUP>12</SUP>CO(J = 1 ─ 0) Line Ratio in Nearby Galaxies
question: Reveal if there are spatial and large-scale radial variations in the 12CO(J=2-1)/12CO(J=1-0) line ratio r21 in nearby galaxies and differences depending on galaxy morphology.

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image, and match resolution of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) TP cubes
recipe.method: Calibrate to antenna temperature scale via chopper-wheel method, remove atmospheric O3 residuals, subtract linear baselines, grid onto HPBW/9 pixels with prolate spheroidal function, compute pairwise relative flux scales across EBs by inverting the design matrix and coadd, smooth CO(2-1) to 56.6" with Gaussian kernel, and bin both cubes to 10 km s-1.
key_parameters: Grid size HPBW/9 (5.62" for CO 10, 2.81" for CO 21), prolate spheroidal support radius 6 pixels
Target beam 56.6", velocity bin 10 km s-1

recipe.goal: Create moment maps, spatial r21 maps, and measure luminosity-weighted r21
recipe.method: Integrate channels with CO detection to make moment 0 maps; create moment 1 maps where moment 0 S/N > 5; measure total flux of both lines within the whole FOV of the CO 21 moment 0 map to compute luminosity-weighted r21; divide moment 0 maps where both lines have S/N > 5 to make spatial r21 maps.
key_parameters: S/N > 5 threshold for moment 1 and spatial r21 map display
assumptions: Absolute flux calibration uncertainty of 2.4% for both CO lines, giving 3% uncertainty in quadrature on luminosity-weighted r21

recipe.goal: Generate major-axis position-velocity (PV) diagrams of r21
recipe.method: Extract PV diagrams along the major axis for CO 10 and CO 21 using CASA impv with a 1' slit width, exclude pixels within 28" of map edges, measure CO 10 PV rms in emission-free regions, and divide the CO 21 PV diagram by the CO 10 PV diagram for regions above 20 sigma (10 sigma for NGC 1512 and NGC 4579).
key_parameters: Slit width = 1', edge exclusion = 28", threshold = 20 sigma (10 sigma for NGC 1512 and NGC 4579)

recipe.goal: Separate circularly rotating disk from kinematic outliers via tilted-ring modeling
recipe.method: Fit the CO 10 cube with a tilted-ring model in 3DBarolo using concentric 28.8" rings, create a major-axis PV diagram from the model cube, and define regions inside the 30 sigma model contour (10 sigma for NGC 1512 and NGC 4579) as 'disk' and regions on/outside as 'outlier'.
key_parameters: Ring width = 28.8", radial gas inflow/outflow fixed to 0, PA, inclination, and rotation velocity free in each ring
Model PV contour threshold = 30 sigma (10 sigma for NGC 1512 and NGC 4579)
assumptions: Pure circular rotation in tilted rings with zero radial inflow/outflow

recipe.goal: Compare r21 distributions and radial profiles across kinematic components and galaxy morphologies
recipe.method: Compute raw and sample-normalized histograms of r21 in PV pixels for disk and outlier components across SA, SAB, and SB classes, perform Welch's t-tests, and compute radial profiles in 5.6" bins normalized by central 28" mean r21, optical radius R25, and bar radius RA2.
key_parameters: Histogram bin width = 0.027; radial bin width = 5.6"; minimum 3 data points per radial bin

evidence.quote: The average value of luminosity-weighted mean is r 21 = 0.61 with a standard deviation of 0.06, consistent with previous studies (Y. Yajima et al. 2021; J. S. den Brok et al. 2021; A. K. Leroy et al. 2022).
Global average values of r 21 = 0.61 ± 0.06 are consistent with averages in the literature.

answer_key.quantity: Mean PV r21 (all galaxies, disk + outlier)

evidence.quote: The average value of r 21 for all our galaxies (disk and outlier combined) is r 21 = 0.63 ± 0.09, which is consistent with the average of the luminosity-weighted mean (0.61 ± 0.06) in Section 3.1.

answer_key.quantity: Mean PV r21 (all galaxies, disk component)

evidence.quote: The outliers have a statistically larger mean value of r 21 = 0.69 ± 0.10 compared to the disk with r 21 = 0.62 ± 0.08.

answer_key.quantity: Mean PV r21 (all galaxies, outlier component)

evidence.quote: The normalized distribution matches the non-normalized distribution very well, and a Welch's t-test between the disk and outliers in the normalized data set gives a p-value of 0.009, indicating that the disk and outliers likely come from different distributions.

score_reason: All ALMA project codes are explicitly listed, the single-dish gridding, smoothing, velocity binning, PV slit widths, S/N thresholds, and 3DBarolo ring widths are clearly stated, and extensive numeric tables are provided; minor deductions for unstated rejected EBs, exact line-window channels per galaxy, and 3DBarolo nuisance parameters.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA TP data (2022.1.00360.S and PHANGS archival projects) are public, TP cube reduction and PV/3DBarolo analysis are computationally lightweight, and Table 1 and Table 3 provide clean numeric benchmarks for luminosity-weighted and kinematic-component r21 values across 11 galaxies.
